exposure: fetal anemia due to congenital parvo B19 infection
fetal anemia due to RBC alloimmunization
outcome: abnormal fetal neuroimaging findings (cerebellar hypoplasia, polymicrogyria, intracranial hemorrhage, severe ventriculomegaly)
cohort: The study included 71 fetuses that required at least one intrauterine blood transfusion (IUT) due to fetal anemia, divided into groups based on the cause of anemia: congenital parvo B19 infection or RBC alloimmunization.
finding: Fetuses with parvo B19-induced anemia treated with IUT showed significantly increased rates of abnormal neuroimaging findings compared to those with RBC alloimmunization (26.7% vs. 3.8%), though there was no difference in long-term neurodevelopmental delay rates between the groups.
followup_time: up to 6.53 years (average age of 3.65 and 6.53 years for assessment)
gest_age: 22.91 ± 3.36 weeks (Parvo B19 group) vs. 27.37 ± 4.67 weeks (RBC alloimmunization group) at presentation for IUT
